owner_design.value: OwnedSigalgs (src/ssl/t1_lib.rs:1015) owns exactly one CRYPTO_malloc block and the element count it was allocated for; the only constructors are from_codes (:1024) and from_scheme_bytes (:1042), each of which allocates the block for exactly codes.len()/count schemes and initialises every slot before the value exists. Its Drop (through OwnedBlock) is the block's single release.
owner_design.transfer_boundary: SigalgsSlot (src/ssl/t1_lib.rs:1071) borrows a connection's two member words. replace (:1098) releases the incumbent and publishes a new list; clear (:1108) releases and publishes (NULL, 0). replace is private to the module, so only an OwnedSigalgs built here can be published; the pair cannot be made to disagree with its allocation through the sanctioned surface.
owner_design.connection_surface: Ssl.peer_sigalgs/peer_sigalgslen and Ssl.shared_sigalgs/shared_sigalgslen are private (src/ssl/ssl_lib.rs:1839-1850). Ssl::peer_sigalgs (:2301) and Ssl::shared_sigalgs (:2325) are safe reads that answer an empty slice for NULL and otherwise derive the extent from the connection's own count; Ssl::peer_sigalgs_slot (:2317) and Ssl::shared_sigalgs_slot (:2339) are unsafe derivations whose contracts require the pair invariant. CtxDestroy releases both through the slots (:3655-3657).
owner_design.shared_list_representation: The negotiated list stores native-endian u16 scheme codes instead of SIGALG_LOOKUP pointers. No exported ABI reads the representation; SSL_get_shared_sigalgs resolves each code through the same static table, so the accessor's NID out-parameters are the authority's lu->hash/lu->sig/lu->sigandhash and rsig/rhash are the code's low/high bytes.
owner_design.callback_safety: tls1_set_shared_sigalgs copies the connection's peer list into a Vec before the shared-list walk invokes the application security callback, so no borrow of connection storage crosses that re-entrancy edge.
owner_design.authority_ordering: A replacement list is allocated before the incumbent is released, preserving tls1_save_u16's parse/allocate-then-store ordering: a refused allocation or a malformed vector leaves the incumbent installed.

eliminated: alloc_peer_sigalgs (manual CRYPTO_free of the incumbent, hand-checked multiply, raw store and separate length write) was removed; allocation and publication are now the OwnedSigalgs constructors plus SigalgsSlot::replace.

Caller-computed (pointer, length) slice construction in SSL_get_sigalgs, SSL_get_shared_sigalgs, tls13_construct_cert_verify, tls12_sign and the client test helper `saved`: all now read one invariant-checked accessor whose extent is the allocation's own count.
Crate-wide mutability of Ssl.peer_sigalgs/shared_sigalgs: both fields are private, so no caller outside the owner/transfer code can publish a length that disagrees with the block.
The direct raw publication of the pair in ssl_lib contract_tests (raw CRYPTO_malloc plus two field writes): now routed through tls1_save_peer_sigalgs_raw.
A re-entrancy hazard in the shared-list walk: the peer list is copied before the application security callback runs, so no connection borrow survives the callback.
relocated: List provenance, extent, alignment and the single release are now OwnedBlock::malloc / OwnedBlock::Drop, reached only through OwnedSigalgs.

The (ptr, len) transfer lifecycle is now SigalgsSlot::replace (release-then-publish a pre-built list) and SigalgsSlot::clear (release and publish NULL/0); CtxDestroy releases both lists through those handles.
The authority's parse/allocate-before-release ordering is retained by building the OwnedSigalgs value before replace() frees the incumbent.
introduced: Private-field invariant: Ssl.peer_sigalgs/peer_sigalgslen and Ssl.shared_sigalgs/shared_sigalgslen are either (NULL, 0) or one exclusively owned CRYPTO_* block of exactly len initialised u16s. Documented on the fields and both safe accessors.
SigalgsSlot::of and SigalgsSlot::clear contracts (live connection member pair; exclusive borrow; incumbent is the connection's own single block).
OwnedSigalgs::from_codes/from_scheme_bytes internal initialisation contracts (every slot written before the value exists; checked extent).
Live-connection contracts on tls12_sigalg_allowed, tls12_shared_sigalgs, tls1_set_shared_sigalgs and tls1_process_sigalgs.

The authority does not clear peer_sigalgs between requests either, so a repeated request without the extension recomputes from the same stale peer list and yields the same answer in the ordinary case; a configuration/security-state change between requests would diverge.
